title: Informal Conjecture on exact asymptotics of maxcode_L for even L
statement_text: We believe that in fact $\mathrm{maxcode}_L(\varepsilon) = c_L \varepsilon^{-1} + O(1)$ for even $L$.
context_text: A binary code $C\subset\{0,1\}^n$ is $<L$-list-decodable with radius $\tau$ if for every word $w\in\{0,1\}^n$ there are fewer than $L$ codewords within Hamming distance $\tau n$ from $w$ (equivalently, no point of the hypercube is covered by $L$ or more of the Hamming balls of relative radius $\tau$ centred at the codewords). Let $\tau_L=\frac{1}{2}-\binom{2k}{k}/2^{2k+1}$ if $L=2k$ or $L=2k+1$. By Blinovsky, for radius below $\tau_L$ the largest such code is exponentially large in $n$, while for radius above $\tau_L$ its size is bounded independently of $n$. For $\varepsilon>0$, $\mathrm{maxcode}_L(\varepsilon)$ is the maximum size $|C|$ of a $<L$-list-decodable code $C\subset\{0,1\}^n$ of radius $\tau_L+\varepsilon$, the maximum being over all block lengths $n$. For $L=2$ (unique decoding) Levenshtein's construction shows $\mathrm{maxcode}_2(\varepsilon)=\frac{1}{4\varepsilon}+O(1)$. The authors prove, for every $L\ge 2$, that $\mathrm{maxcode}_L(\varepsilon)\ge c_L\varepsilon^{-1}+O(1)$ where $c_L=2^{-L}\lfloor L/2\rfloor\binom{L-1}{\lfloor L/2\rfloor}$, and that $\mathrm{maxcode}_L(\varepsilon)=O(\varepsilon^{-1})$ when $L$ is even; the conjecture says the lower bound is tight up to an additive constant for even $L$. For odd $L$ the behaviour differs: they prove $\mathrm{maxcode}_3(\varepsilon)=\Theta(\varepsilon^{-3/2})$, refuting a claimed $O(1/\varepsilon)$ bound of Blinovsky.
